items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: The interviewee discusses Jelly Roll Morton (a New Orleans musician) in the context of historical research and recording, stating 'I don't know who suggested... to Lomax that he record Jelly talking about New Orleans history'.

ctx.x: So there wasn't, you see, much interest there either. I mean, people didn't even know Jelly was there. A fellow by the name of Sidney Martin was probably the first one that discovered that Jelly was in Washington. And he wrote a little piece, maybe only a couple of inches long column or so on Jelly in Downbeat. And Charles Smith was down there soon after that working for the government. And anyway, I don't know who suggested, it might be that it was Sidney Martin that suggested, I think, to Lomax that he record…
And to your knowledge, that's the first taped interview, I guess you could say it was in a way, of any New Orleans musician. Or would that be fair to say, the first oral history you've done?

Possibly. Possibly that it was recorded, at least. As far as I know. It might have been something. It wasn't taped, of course, they didn't have tape until after the World War II in this country. But it was done as Lomax once mentioned to him, he was on a broken down Presto, he called it. Which, of course, unfortunately didn't run the right speed. It was running a little too slow, I guess it was, or something. Anyway, the pitch came out wrong. Which makes the thing too high, I guess, when you play it back at, say,…
